title: Knockin' on Heaven's Door
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
techniqueFocus: G to D to Am changes
notes: Whole song is one 8-bar loop (G D Am / G D C). Every chart agrees. Many players use Am7 or C as Cadd9 for smoother changes.

title: Bad Moon Rising
strummingPattern: D DU UDU
techniqueFocus: quick A-to-G change inside one bar
notes: Verse bar 2 splits A and G (two beats each). Chorus: 2 bars G, 2 bars D, 1 A, 1 G, 2 D. Hooktheory and Lauren Bateman agree; tempo about 180 bpm.

title: Brown Eyed Girl
strummingPattern: D DU UDU
notes: Recording opens with a lead-guitar riff over G C G D; strumming those chords works. JustinGuitar and Heartwood agree on the C D G Em C D G D chorus. The refrain is often shown with D7.

title: Stand By Me
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: Recording is in A (A F#m D E). The usual guitar version uses capo 2 with G Em C D shapes. Without a capo, play A F#m D E.

title: Let It Be
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
techniqueFocus: small F or Fmaj7 as a stepping stone
notes: Piano-led recording in C with no capo. Some charts write passing F/A or C/G bass walks; the core shapes are always C G Am F.

title: Take Me Home, Country Roads
strummingPattern: D DU UDU
notes: Recording is in A. Capo 2 with G-shapes is the standard learner version; the e-chords and UG charts agree. The bridge D is often played as D7.

title: I'm Yours
album: We Sing. We Dance. We Steal Things.
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: Recording sounds in B. Popular charts use either capo 4 with C G Am F or half-step-down tuning with the same shapes; both sound the same. Some charts write the chorus F as F with a D7 turnaround. Strum with a skank/chop feel; the tempo can be counted as 76 half-time.

title: Let Her Go
strummingPattern: D D D U D U
notes: Passenger plays capo 7 with G-major shapes, so it sounds in D. Heartwood and National Guitar Academy agree on the sections. Bm is the only barre chord; a Bm7 or a mini Bm works.

title: Perfect
strummingPattern: D - D U D U
techniqueFocus: Em7 to Csus2 voicings with anchor fingers
notes: Capo 1 with G shapes, sounding in G#/Ab. Bell & Co and Fender agree. The recording uses Em7/Csus2 voicings; plain Em/C is fine for beginners. 12/8 at about 63 bpm (dotted quarter), often felt as 95.

title: Riptide
strummingPattern: D D U U D U
notes: Capo 1 with Am G C shapes (sounds C#/Db). Guitaring.net, ozbcoz and Glanworth agree. F (or Fmaj7) appears only in the build/bridge. Chord changes come on beat 4 in some bars, so practise slowly.

title: Blowin' in the Wind
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: Sounds in D. Dylan actually played G-shapes with capo 7 (dylanchords.com); this chart uses the no-capo D shapes from Bell & Co, which sound the same. Em is often skipped in simplified charts.

title: Stick Season
strummingPattern: D D D U D U
notes: Sounds in A. Lauren Bateman uses capo 2 with G D Em C; ChordsWorld and e-chords show A E F#m D with no capo, which is the same. Lauren's chorus adds a passing E shape near the end; the loop above is the common version.

title: Wonderwall
strummingPattern: D DU UDU
techniqueFocus: anchor fingers on B and e strings
notes: Capo 2 standard. UG and GuitarPlayerBox agree. Ring fingers 3 and 4 stay on frets 3 of B and e for every shape. Dsus4 is often written Dsus4/F#.

title: Photograph
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
techniqueFocus: Bm barre in a pop loop
dynamic build from picked verse to strummed chorus
notes: Sounds in E. Sources split between capo 2 (D Bm A G) and capo 4 (C Am G F); both sound in E. We use the capo 2 version.

title: Someone Like You
strummingPattern: D D D D
notes: Piano original in A. Capo 2 with G-shapes is standard (UG, GuitarPlayerBox, guitardownunder). Arpeggiate eighth notes to copy the piano; Bm/F# can be simplified to Bm.

title: Yellow
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
techniqueFocus: ringing open strings over moving bass
notes: Recording in B (B, F#6, Emaj7). Most learner charts use capo 4 with G D C(maj7) shapes. Chris Martin's own voicings keep the top strings ringing (sus/add shapes). Bar lengths in the verse vary a little between charts.

title: Viva La Vida
album: Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends
strummingPattern: D D U D U
notes: Capo 1 with C D G Em shapes, sounding in G#/Ab (Db Eb Ab Fm). UG and GuitarTabsExplorer agree. Bm (the last chorus line) is the only barre chord.

title: Shape of You
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: One loop the whole way: C#m F#m A B in C#m. JustinGuitar and GuitarPlayerBox both use capo 4 with Am Dm F G. Rhythm matters more than chords; mute on beats 2 and 4.

title: Counting Stars
strummingPattern: D DU UDU
notes: Sounds C#m E B A. Capo 4 with Am C G F (Bell & Co, guitaretab). Same loop all song; the challenge is keeping the 16th strum going at full speed.

title: Wake Me Up
strummingPattern: D DU UDU
notes: Bm (i-VI-III-VII) at 124 bpm, per Hooktheory and UG. Some charts use capo 2 Am F C G (same sound). Hooktheory notes the verse leaves out the A on some passes; holding D is fine.

title: Stay With Me
strummingPattern: D - D - D - D U
notes: Sounds in C (Am F C loop). e-chords uses no capo with Am F C; Bell & Co uses capo 5 with Em C G, which is the same. Chorus bar 5 is sometimes G7 or G/B.

title: Hallelujah
strummingPattern: D - - D U D
notes: Cohen's recording is in C (JustinGuitar, National Guitar Academy). Jeff Buckley's cover is also often played in C. Count in 6/8 or 12/8; some charts write E instead of E7.

title: Wish You Were Here
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
techniqueFocus: D/F# with thumb or bass note
notes: Standard tuning, no capo. JustinGuitar, Lauren Bateman and UG agree. The intro has a single-note lead riff; strumming the chord loop is enough to play along.

title: Hey There Delilah
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: Key D at 104 bpm (Tunebat, Musicnotes). UG and Chordify charts use D F#m Bm G A with no capo. The recording is fingerpicked; strumming works for beginners. The pre-chorus A-G-A turnaround is left out here.

title: Hotel California
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: Played in Bm with barre chords (National Guitar Academy, Lauren Bateman). Don Felder's 12-string uses capo 7 with Am E G D F C Dm E shapes, which sound the same. The single was released in 1977; the album came out in December 1976.

title: Sweet Child O' Mine
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: Guitars are tuned down a half step (Eb standard), so D shapes sound C#/Db; capo stays 0. Played in standard tuning, the shapes sound a half step higher than the record. GuitarTabsExplorer and Songsterr agree on the chords. The famous intro is a single-note riff over these chords.

title: Creep
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
techniqueFocus: dynamic muted verse to loud chorus
notes: G B C Cm loop the whole song, G major at 92 bpm (songbpm, Chordify). The B and Cm barres are the challenge. Single 1992, album 1993.

title: More Than Words
strummingPattern: D - X - D U X U
notes: Nuno Bettencourt tunes down a half step, so G shapes sound F#; capo 0. Some charts use standard tuning (sounds in G) or capo shapes. Tempo is about 90-95 bpm; sources vary. Many voicings and fast changes.

title: Tears in Heaven
strummingPattern: D - D U - U D U
notes: Main sections in A; the bridge moves to G before returning (Jon MacLennan, UG). F#m is often F#m7. Slash chords define the bass line; detection may hear A/E as A.

title: The House of the Rising Sun
strummingPattern: D DU DU
notes: Am C D F / Am C E E / Am C D F / Am E Am E (Applied Guitar Theory, UG). 6/8; tempo is quoted as 117-125. Rated advanced for the full-barre F and a steady 6/8 arpeggio; the chords alone are intermediate. The outro chord before the end is sometimes Dm.
